problems.quote: organised by the Goa University Department of Konkani
problems.problem: Goa University was established in 1985; no such department existed in 1974.
problems.correction: organised by the Konkani department of the Goa Post-Graduate Centre
problems.verifierReason: Goa University founded 1985; 1974 event would be under Goa Post-Graduate Centre (CPIR), its predecessor.

problems.quote: classification of fundamental rights into justiciable and non‑justiciable categories
problems.problem: Fundamental rights are justiciable; directive principles are non‑justiciable. The classification is between fundamental rights and directive principles, not within fundamental rights.
problems.correction: classification of constitutional provisions into justiciable fundamental rights and non‑justiciable directive principles
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates classification; fundamental rights are justiciable, directive principles non-justiciable. Correction accurately reflects this.

problems.quote: Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981) introduced the “doctrine of prospective overruling” to protect amendments made before 24 April 1973.
problems.problem: The doctrine of prospective overruling was not introduced in Waman Rao; it was used earlier (e.g., Golaknath, Kesavananda). Waman Rao applied it to protect pre‑1973 amendments.
problems.correction: Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981) applied the doctrine of prospective overruling to protect amendments made before 24 April 1973.
problems.verifierReason: Waman Rao applied, not introduced, prospective overruling. Correction correctly states application to pre-1973 amendments.

problems.quote: In State of Rajasthan v. Union of India (1977) the Court struck down a notification issued beyond the rule‑making power conferred by the enabling Act.
problems.problem: State of Rajasthan v. Union of India (1977) dealt with President's rule under Article 356, not delegated legislation. The case cited is incorrect for the proposition.
problems.correction: In a delegated legislation case, the Court struck down a notification issued beyond the rule‑making power conferred by the enabling Act.
problems.verifierReason: State of Rajasthan v. Union of India (1977) concerns Art. 356, not delegated legislation. Correction states valid general principle without error.

problems.quote: National Thermal Power Corporation v. Singer Company (1992) the Supreme Court interpreted a bilateral investment treaty
problems.problem: The case National Thermal Power Corporation v. Singer Company (1992) dealt with a contract for supply of steam turbines, not a bilateral investment treaty.
problems.correction: National Thermal Power Corporation v. Singer Company (1992) concerned a contract for supply of equipment
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates case as BIT interpretation; it was a contract for steam turbines. Correction correctly describes it as equipment supply contract.

problems.quote: Entry 51 of the Union List

problems.correction: Entry 51 of the State List
problems.verifierReason: Tax on liquor sale is State subject under State List Entry 51, not Union List. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: 2019 National Education Policy

problems.correction: 2020 National Education Policy

problems.correction: communities in Mumbai, Mangalore, and the Gulf

problems.problem: Wrong case attribution. Kumar v. Union of India (1995) 3 SCC 214 deals with Order 2 Rule 2 CPC (splitting of cause of action/constructive res judicata), not issue estoppel. The leading Supreme Court authority on issue estoppel is State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain (1977) (also M.S. Sheriff v. State of M
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain (1977) clarified that issue estoppel applies only when the issue was essential to the previous judgment and the parties are the same or their privie
problems.verifierReason: Kumar v. UOI (1995) concerns O.2 R.2 CPC, not issue estoppel. Nawab Hussain (1977) is the correct authority.

problems.quote: If the issue was decided in a prior criminal proceeding, the analysis shifts to issue estoppel with reference to Kumar.
problems.problem: Wrong case reference for issue estoppel in criminal proceedings. The leading case is State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain (1977), which directly addresses issue estoppel arising from a criminal acquittal in a subsequent departmental proceeding. Kumar v. Union of India (1995) is not the relevant authority.

problems.quote: Section 511 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) punishes attempts to commit offences punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years or more.
problems.problem: Section 511 applies to offences punishable with imprisonment for life or any term of imprisonment, not limited to "up to seven years or more".
problems.correction: Section 511 of the IPC punishes attempts to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or any term.
problems.verifierReason: Section 511 applies to offences punishable with life or any imprisonment, not limited to 'up to seven years or more'; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: mere preparation does not attract punishment under IPC Section 43 (which covers preparation to commit murder).
problems.problem: Section 43 IPC defines terms like "illegal" and "legally bound to do"; it does not cover preparation to commit murder. There is no general IPC provision punishing mere preparation.
problems.correction: mere preparation does not attract punishment under the IPC (no general provision punishes mere preparation).
problems.verifierReason: Section 43 IPC is a definition section, not about preparation for murder; no general preparation offence exists; correction correct.

problems.quote: while murder carries life imprisonment or death, attempted murder carries only up to seven years.
problems.problem: Attempted murder under Section 307 IPC carries up to 10 years, or life imprisonment if hurt is caused.
problems.correction: while murder carries life imprisonment or death, attempted murder carries up to ten years or life if hurt caused.
problems.verifierReason: Attempted murder under Section 307 carries up to 10 years (or life if hurt caused), not up to 7; correction accurate.

problems.quote: attempting robbery attracts punishment under Section 511 read with Section 302/323
problems.problem: Attempted robbery is specifically punished under Section 393 IPC (up to 7 years), not under Section 511 read with Sections 302/323.
problems.correction: attempting robbery attracts punishment under Section 393 (up to seven years).
problems.verifierReason: Attempted robbery is specifically punished under Section 393, not under Section 511 with 302/323; correction accurate.

problems.quote: unless the object of the conspiracy is an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for two years or more, in which case an overt act is necessary
problems.problem: For criminal conspiracy to commit an offence, no overt act is required under Section 120A proviso; an overt act is required only for conspiracy to do an illegal act not amounting to an offence.
problems.correction: unless the object is an illegal act not amounting to an offence, in which case an overt act is necessary.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates overt act requirement for conspiracy; correction correctly states overt act needed only for illegal act not amounting to offence.

problems.quote: ദളിത് സാഹിത്യം — Dalit writing from the 1990s
problems.problem: Dalit writing in Malayalam began well before the 1990s (e.g., Poykayil Appachan, Kallen Pokkudan); the 1990s mark a more organized movement, not the origin.
problems.correction: ദളിത് സാഹിത്യം — Dalit writing from early 20th century, organised movement from 1990s
problems.verifierReason: Dalit writing in Malayalam predates 1990s; early 20th century origins correct, 1990s marks organised movement.
